answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by tying each identity to locked stake and a non-transferable work history: a new agent must complete verified tasks before handling valuable work, like a crystal growing one layer at a time. A prism check then splits any claimed history into separate proofs - task receipts, peer attestations, and stake locks - so clones show mismatched fragments. Adding one fake identity means paying fresh stake and waiting again, so a thousand-copy attack costs a thousand times more than one honest agent, while a copied pigment of reputation alone buys nothing.
